subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should OpenClaw narrow host workspace override propagation for third-party managed npm plugin roots, add targeted Express 4/path-to-regexp conflict validation, or keep the current propagation policy and require plugin-local overrides?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the permanent fix changes the dependency ownership boundary for third-party plugins and may trade plugin compatibility against centrally enforced security overrides.

options.title: Scoped conflict policy
options.body: Preserve security overrides by default but add a narrow conflict policy for plugin-owned dependency graphs, with tests for Express 4 and OpenClaw's Express 5/router path.

options.title: Validator only
options.body: Keep current override propagation and add a clear install/startup diagnostic telling Express 4 plugin authors to ship a package-local override or migrate.

options.title: Plugin-owned dependencies win
options.body: Stop applying broad host overrides into third-party plugin roots, accepting that some central security pins no longer automatically cover external plugins.

recommendation.title: Scoped conflict policy
recommendation.body: Preserve security overrides by default but add a narrow conflict policy for plugin-owned dependency graphs, with tests for Express 4 and OpenClaw's Express 5/router path.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the merged PR that introduced the managed external plugin override propagation now implicated by the issue.
